children: New Delhi, Oct. 12 -- Amid a 'red alert' for thunderstorms across Delhi-NCR, the Delhi Airport on Monday issued a travel advisory warning travellers of possible flight disruptions due to "adverse weather conditions" in its vicinity.
However, no flight delays were reported at the time of publishing.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a 'red' alert, warning of thunderstorms, lightning, gusty winds reaching up to 60 kmph, and heavy rainfall exceeding 15 mm per hour across the national capital region-including Gurugram, Faridabad, Noida, and Ghaziabad.

"As per the IMD's forecast, inclement weather conditions are expected in the vicinity of Delhi Airport," Delhi Airport said in its advisory. "However, flight operations at Delhi Airport are currently normal."
"Our on-ground teams are working diligently with all stakeholders to ensure your journey remains hassle-free," it added.

In a separate tweet, the Delhi Airport requested passengers to pay attention to the traffic advisory today, ahead of the INDIA bloc's planned protest march to the Supreme Court against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
According to the Delhi Traffic Police advisory, traffic will be heavily regulated, and diversions could impact several arterial roads, roundabouts, and flyovers across Central and New Delhi.
Passengers headed to Indira Gandhi International Airport have been advised to "please keep extra travel time in hand if heading towards the airport via New Delhi and Central Delhi."
SpiceJet also cautioned that departures, arrivals, and subsequent flights could be affected by the heavy rains in Delhi-NCR.

"Due to bad weather (heavy rain) in Delhi (DEL), all departures/arrivals and their consequential flights might be affected," the airline said, urging the passengers to check their flight status before heading to the airport.
In the national capital, intense morning downpours and thunderstorms led to water accumulation on several low-lying roads, notably near the Jhandewalan Temple area in Karol Bagh.
The Safdarjung observatory, which provides representative data for Delhi, recorded 40 mm of rainfall till 5.30 am, and the Delhi airport received 30 mm, according to IMD data.

Over the past 24 hours, maximum temperatures across Delhi dipped by 1 to 2 degrees Celsius, hovering between 30 and 32 degrees Celsius, while minimum temperatures settled between 21 and 24 degrees Celsius.
Overall daytime highs are projected to remain between 31 and 35 degrees Celsius over the coming week as sunny to partly cloudy conditions resume.
The IMD forecast indicates that the wet spell will be brief, predicting partly cloudy skies and dry conditions across Delhi for the next six days.
